title: A projection of irrational trace and the Baum–Connes conjecture
author: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic)
description: An exposition of OpenAI's construction (2026) of a finitely generated group G_sur and a projection b_0 in its reduced group C*-algebra whose canonical trace is the irrational number sum_i p^(-k_i). With Lück's theorem on traces of assembly classes, the class of b_0 is not in the image of the Baum-Connes assembly map, so the reduced Baum-Connes conjecture without coefficients fails for G_sur. The first lesson sets up traces of projections and K_0, states the conjecture and Lück's theorem, and deduces the failure; the second to fourth build a graphical small cancellation group Gamma whose Cayley graph contains labelled expanders, and prove avoidance, thin triangles with a universal constant, the simultaneous overlap bound and the direct sum decomposition of its cycle space; the fifth builds the module V from linear codes with large primal and dual distance and proves that the pattern on each copy is uniform on its code; the sixth and seventh prove the Fourier decomposition, the deficit estimates, the uniform spectral gap of the random subgraph Laplacians and the trace formula.
prerequisites: programme course Foundations of von Neumann algebras: lesson C*-algebras, continuous functional calculus, automatic continuity and positive cones (Theorems 3.2 and 5.1, Corollaries 4.6 and 5.4)
programme course The Kervaire conjecture (the-kervaire-conjecture): lesson The regular trace and spectral phase (Lemmas 1.1 and 1.3)
core course Measure and Integration (D10): infinite products of probability spaces (Fremlin, Measure Theory, Volume 2, Section 254)

open_obligations: Named statements used without proof in the course: (VK) van Kampen diagrams: a word that is a product of N conjugates of relators has a diagram with at most N faces, the boundary walk is a product of conjugates of the face walks, and a diagram has a unique label-preserving map to the Cayley graph from any base point (Bridson, The geometry of the word problem, Definition 4.1.1, Proposition 4.1.2, Theorem 4.2.2 and Section 4.3); (MAP) plane maps: face boundary walks and Euler's formula, deleting an edge between two faces or with both sides on one face, contracting an edge (Erickson, Computational Topology, Sections 9.4, 9.5, 10.2, 10.4 and 10.6) (both in the lesson Graphical presentations and coned diagrams, Section 3); (HYP) a graph in which every closed walk of length n is a product of at most Kn conjugates of closed walks of length at most M has D(K,M)-thin geodesic triangles (Belolipetsky-Paula, Introducao a Teoria Geometrica de Grupos, arXiv:2409.17797, Teorema 8.22; the passage from products of conjugates to fillings as in the proof of Proposition 2.3 of the manuscript) (lesson Thin triangles and simultaneous overlaps, Section 2); (EXP) the Cayley graphs of SL_2(F_p), p >= 5, with respect to (1 3; 0 1), (1 0; 3 1) and their inverses are connected simple 4-regular graphs with a uniform spectral gap and girth at least a constant times log p (Lubotzky, Expander graphs in pure and applied mathematics, arXiv:1105.2389, Theorem 2.21 and the paragraph after it, Propositions 1.3 and 1.5); (OSA) Osajda's small cancellation labelling of a sequence of graphs of bounded degree, girth tending to infinity and diameter at most a constant times the girth, with the uniqueness of long paths and isometric maps into the Cayley graph (Osajda, Small cancellation labellings of some infinite graphs and applications, arXiv:1406.5015, Theorem 2.7, Lemma 3.1 and Theorem 3.2) (both in the lesson Labelled expanders and cycle spaces); (LUCK) Lück's theorem that the trace of every class in the image of the Baum-Connes assembly map lies in Z[1/|F| : F finite subgroup] (Lück, The relation between the Baum-Connes conjecture and the trace conjecture, Invent. Math. 149 (2002), Theorem 0.3, on the author's university page); used only for the consequence on the Baum-Connes conjecture; the assembly map is not constructed in the programme (first lesson, Section 3).
The lessons were written and checked by one model in one session; they have not been checked by a second reader.
